summary: Culver City packs roughly 40,000 people into just five square miles, yet it operates less like a suburb and more like a self-contained job center — Sony Pictures has headquartered here for decades, Amazon Studios moved major operations into the old Culver Studios lot, and Apple TV+ planted a sizable footprint nearby, meaning entertainment-industry workers can sometimes commute by bicycle instead of grinding through the 405. That employment density matters when you look at the housing math: the median home value sits around $1.13 million against a median household income of about $122,000 — a price-to-income ratio above 9:1, which pushes ownership out of reach at median earnings and keeps median rent near $2,700 a month. The Ballona Creek bike path and proximity to the Baldwin Hills scenic overlook offer genuine outdoor escapes without driving, and the flat-to-gently-rolling terrain makes walking practical across a surprisingly connected street grid, with Washington Boulevard and the downtown stretch hosting a dense lineup of independent restaurants, coffee shops, and a respected weekly farmers' market. Sunshine averages 9.5 hours a day with highs around 73°F year-round, so the mild, dry consistency becomes almost invisible — a backdrop rather than an event. Property crime runs notably high at roughly 6,470 per 100,000, driven largely by larceny, which is worth weighing against the walkability and urban convenience. Culver City is essentially a small city that borrowed the job base and energy of a much larger one while keeping a five-mile footprint — and the cost of entry reflects exactly that tension.
